subject: getting the importance value after modelavg

messages.author: af2b16d60afe57cd
messages.subject: getting the importance value after modelavg
parts:
Dear members,


I am trying to investigate spatial and temporal segregation of jackals in relation to other groups and habitat covariates. I want to see how the “abundance” of different vertebrate groups (that are related to jackal´s ecology) influence its habitat use. In other words, I would like to see if jackals tend to use more sites where the abundance of large carnivores is greater/lower for example (I just used a standardized measure of relative abundance as a proxy for the intensity of use -i.e capture rates, to help us develop further hypothesis…).


Since I am more interested in the effect of each of the covariates rather than a particular model, I decided to run a model average (also because each individual model developed very low w), and now I want to calculate the importance of each automatically, however, I am receiving some errors (script below). I have a lot of models after using the “dredge” function to assess all possible combinations (5 covariates for psi). I am following the recommendations from  Marc J. Mazerolle in R (?importance).


So,


1) Could anyone provide feedback/advice as to why I am getting the below errors? Does this have to be with the possibility that during selection (w>90) I might have ended up with different # of models with the variable and without the variable? The error message does not suggest anything related.


2) Do you think it is completely fine just to compare the b coefficients and look at the CI to determine whether one covariate has a stronger effect with respect to the others, having in mind that the variables are all scaled?


Thank you very much in advance.

 

Best regards

L

---------

# global model

M_global_spp <-occu(~ cam_days*code_loc

                    ~ freq_large_carniv + freq_medium_carniv +

                      freq_medium_ungu + freq_large_ungu + freq_extra_large_ungu, umf_spp)

 

#candidate model set (including overdispersion parameter)

cand_Mod_spp_2_Q <- dredge(M_global_spp, extra="R^2", rank="QAICc", chat=1.31)                 

 

#Select models by weight to average

model_sel_90a <- get.models(cand_Mod_spp_2_Q, subset = cumsum(weight) <= 0.90)

 

# average models based on model weights

avg_spp_90a <- model.avg(model_sel_90a, fit = TRUE)

 

#model importance

listcand_Mglobal <- list(model_sel_90a)  #candidate models already defined, must be a list

 

#selecting the models that were included in the model avg

Modenames <- model_sel_90a[c("196","195","212", "204", "68", "211", "67", "203", "228", "227",       "200","84",  "83", "220", "76", "75", "219", "244", "72", "243", "99", "100", "236", "131",   "132", "235", "216", "148", "147", "92", "208", "88", "19", "91","232",

                             "116", "20", "115", "107", "108")]

 

#compute importance value for "freq_large_carniv" on psi

# using pack “AICcmodavg” and R help for ?importancce

 

occ_avg_spp_c <- importance(cand.set = listcand_Mglobal, modnames = Modenames,

                            parm = "freq_large_carniv", parm.type = "psi") ## not working

Error in importance(cand.set = model, modnames = Modenames, parm = "freq_large_carniv",  :

  unused arguments (cand.set = model, modnames = Modenames, parm = "freq_large_carniv", parm.type = "psi")

 

#alternative, from get models

importance(cand.set =model_sel_90a, parm = "freq_large_carniv", modnames = NULL,

           second.ord = TRUE, nobs = NULL, c.hat = 1.3, parm.type = "psi")

 

Error in importance(cand.set = model_sel_90a, parm = "freq_large_carniv",  : 
  unused arguments (cand.set = model_sel_90a, parm = "freq_large_carniv", modnames = NULL, second.ord = TRUE, nobs = NULL, c.hat = 1.3, parm.type = "psi")

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] getting the importance value after modelavg
parts:
Hi Lain,

1) Regarding the error you report, the reason is that packages MuMIn
and AICcmodavg both have a function named importance( ). The package
that is loaded last masks the function of the same name of the other
package. If you load MuMIn first, and then load AICcmodavg when you are
ready to use the functions in the package, then it should work.

2) Model-averaging the beta estimates with the shrinkage estimator
(using the entire set of models) would give you the answer here,
provided each variable appears in the models with the same frequency.
You can also model-average predictions across each model for a given
explanatory variable to plot its effect along with CI's.

Best,

Marc

Hi Marc,

Thanks much for your quick response. It seems to be working.

Now, I received the message “Importance values are only meaningful when the number of models with and without parameter are equal” Then, I imagine, I better implement the shrinkage estimator as you recommended.  I´ll explore that option. 

Thank you very much,

 

Best regards

Lain
